name: Femoral Shaft Fracture
definition: Fracture of the femoral diaphysis, commonly from high-energy trauma in younger adults or fragility/pathological mechanisms in older patients.

investigations.principle: AP/lateral femur radiographs including hip and knee are required; CT is used for associated injuries.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, infection, tumor or occult-injury assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Adult femoral shaft fractures commonly require operative fixation; search for associated injuries.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Bhagna management may complement recovery after modern stabilization.

patientEducation.summary: Fracture of the femoral diaphysis, commonly from high-energy trauma in younger adults or fragility/pathological mechanisms in older patients.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, major trauma, suspected infection, pathological fracture, neurovascular compromise or other listed red flags.
